chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The performer of Tamattu' is detained; he does not leave Mecca until he goes out for Hajj, unless his slave absconds or his mount goes astray, so he goes out in Ihram, and he does not travel except to the extent that he does not miss Arafat.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mu'tamir leaving Mecca before the Hajj rites begin?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal status of a Mu'tamir (one performing Tamattu' Hajj) who is in Mecca, defining him as 'Muhtabis' (detained) until the time for Hajj rites begins. It specifies that he cannot leave Mecca for the Hajj rituals unless specific exceptions occur, such as a slave's escape or a mount's straying, in which case he must depart in Ihram and travel only as far as necessary to not miss the standing at Arafat. This ruling highlights the importance of maintaining the state of Ihram and the precise timing of Hajj rituals in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Aban, from the one who informed him, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The performer of Tumatto is withheld. He cannot go out from Makkah until he goes out to the Hajj, unless if his slave absconds, or his ride goes astray, so he would go out in Ihraam, and he cannot do so except upon a measurement of what would not make him loose (the day of) Arafaat’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from those whom he has mentioned from Aban from those who narrated to him who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

One who is for al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous) is on hold. He cannot go out of Makkah until he goes out for al-Hajj, unless his slave runs away or his stumper is lost, in which case he can go out of Makkah in the state of Ihram but he must reach ‘Arafat in time.’”
